evals.name: fresh-install-withholds-verdicts
evals.prompt: I just set up Claude Code a couple of days ago and I have about 200 skills installed. Which ones am I not using?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to answer the question as asked. Reports the observed horizon (a few days), states that it is far below the exposure floor, and resolves every skill to not-observable with the declined claims listed in the withheld section. Explains that a store younger than the window cannot distinguish never-invoked from never-observed, so a 'you use 3 of 200' answer would be an artifact of install age rather than a finding.
expectations: Output reports an observed horizon and compares it against the exposure floor before making any cold claim
Output resolves rows to not-observable rather than never-used or unused
Output surfaces the withheld section with a reason rather than silently omitting the declined claims
Output does not produce a ranked list of unused skills from a horizon that cannot support one

evals.name: plugin-usage-is-not-skill-usage
evals.prompt: My ~/.claude.json says the guardrails plugin has usageCount 105 and context-guard has 98. Those are my most-used skills, right?
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: pluginUsage counts hook, agent, MCP, and LSP dispatch, not skill invocation, and those two plugins are hook-heavy infrastructure whose skills may never have been invoked at all. Also notes that pluginUsage rows are seeded at install with usageCount 0 beside a current lastUsedAt, so recency read off that field is meaningless unless the count is above zero.
expectations: Output states that pluginUsage counts hook/agent/MCP/LSP dispatch rather than skill invocation
Output declines to present those numbers as skill usage
Output explains that lastUsedAt is seeded at install and is not evidence of use unless usageCount is greater than zero

evals.name: starved-is-not-unwanted
evals.prompt: There are a bunch of skills I keep meaning to use and Claude never suggests them. Should I just delete them?
evals.expected_output: Explains the starvation loop before recommending anything: the skill listing is budgeted at a fraction of the context window, and on overflow Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the least-invoked skills, so a skill at zero usage loses the keywords that would let it be matched and stays at zero. Distinguishes starved-but-wanted from genuinely unwanted, and does not recommend deletion on the strength of low usage alone.
expectations: Output explains the budget-and-drop mechanism rather than treating low usage as a preference signal
Output separates starved from genuinely unwanted
Output does not recommend deleting skills solely because they show no usage

evals.name: routes-away-from-the-shipped-feature
evals.prompt: Just show me which skills are unused and how much context they cost me.
evals.expected_output: Routes to Claude Code's own /doctor and Stats tab, which already report unused skills against their context cost, and explains that this skill answers the adjacent question — why they are unused, and whether the listing budget is suppressing them — rather than duplicating that report.
expectations: Output names Claude Code's own /doctor or Stats tab as the owner of the unused-vs-context-cost question
Output states what this skill adds instead of duplicating that report
